query: What signals suggest a support ticket will take longer to resolve?

per_column.name: has_technical_issue
per_column.rationale: Derived from issue_description, this flags problem type known at ticket intake. Technical issues plausibly take longer to resolve and it lies outside resolution_minutes with no leakage.

per_column.name: is_customer_blocked
per_column.rationale: Indicates severity/urgency knowable from the initial ticket text. Carries plausible predictive signal about resolution time without restating or leaking the outcome.

per_column.name: needs_investigation
per_column.rationale: Signals complexity requiring diagnostic effort, inferable from the description. Investigation-heavy tickets plausibly take longer; it is a legitimate upstream predictor.

per_column.name: has_external_integration
per_column.rationale: Involvement of third-party systems is a structural attribute derivable from the description and plausibly increases resolution time. Outside the focus, no leakage.

per_column.name: affects_multiple_users
per_column.rationale: Scope/blast-radius indicator knowable at intake, plausibly correlated with longer resolution. It is a valid predictor, not a component or restatement of the focus.

judge.rationale: All five added columns are binary features extracted from the issue_description text, each capturing a distinct facet of ticket complexity/scope (technical nature, customer-blocking, investigation need, external dependencies, breadth of impact). None restates or is a deterministic function of resolution_minutes, and all are knowable at intake, so there is no leakage. As a set they add genuine incremental signal beyond priority/channel/agent by mining the free-text field. Utility is strong but not maximal: the flags are coarse binary indicators with unspecified extraction reliability and likely mutual correlation, and observed distributions for several are quite skewed, limiting marginal leverage.
